name: Wendigo Mane
summary: Across Dun Morogh, wendigo manes are gathered from the beasts roaming its frozen crags. Their thick coats offer warmth against the mountain cold, and Pilot Stonegear has a use for them.

sections.title: Warmth for the Ironworks
sections.body: Dun Morogh’s wendigos roam the snowdrifts, and their coarse fur shields against bitter drafts. Pilot Stonegear, stationed outside Kharanos, sends adventurers to Grizzled Den for their heavy manes. He plans to weave them into an insulating floor rug for the interior deck of his prized dwarven siege engine, Trollplow.

faq.q: What creatures yield a Wendigo Mane?
faq.answer: Wendigo manes come from wendigos in the snows of Dun Morogh, including Young Wendigos, adult Wendigos, and alpha beasts such as Vagash, Edan the Howler, and Old Icebeard.

faq.q: Why does Pilot Stonegear want these manes?
faq.answer: Pilot Stonegear wants the manes to make an insulating rug for the interior deck of his siege engine, Trollplow. The thick fur will help keep his station warm as the machine travels through frozen terrain.

faq.q: Where is the best place to find wendigos for their manes?
faq.answer: Pilot Stonegear recommends Grizzled Den, a cave system cut into the mountains directly west of Kharanos. Wendigos fill the cavern and its surrounding slopes.
Yes. Wendigos are feral, territorial predators with great strength and thick hides. Dwarven trainers regard facing them in their dens as an early test of a mountaineer’s courage and fighting grit.

angles.text: Dwarven machinery in Dun Morogh has freezing metal cockpits, so wendigo pelts make practical insulating linings.
Young dwarves hunt the wendigos of Grizzled Den to prove their toughness to Kharanos veterans.
